tagline: A short designated link from Russell Cave Road to Paris Pike
intro: Hughes Lane connects Russell Cave Road with Paris Pike in Fayette County. Kentucky’s scenic-highway inventory gives the lane a length of 2.220 miles and a designation date of November 20, 1996. The designated Russell Cave Road segment ends at Hughes Lane.

At the other end is Paris Pike, the US 27/68 corridor between Lexington and Paris. That highway’s widening began in 1997 and was completed in 2003. Hughes Lane’s designated drive runs from KY 353 to the US 27/68 intersection.

moments.title: Russell Cave Road junction
moments.text: Hughes Lane’s designated route starts at KY 353, Russell Cave Road. Russell Cave Road has its own scenic designation, covering the segment from Ironworks Pike to this junction.

moments.title: Hughes Lane
moments.text: The scenic inventory treats Hughes Lane as its own 2.220-mile route in Fayette County. Its November 20, 1996 designation shares official order 97404 with Russell Cave Road.

moments.title: Paris Pike junction
moments.text: Hughes Lane ends at US 27/68, Paris Pike. Paris Pike’s widening project began in 1997 and finished in 2003. On Paris Pike, dry-laid limestone fences were dismantled and rebuilt by hand during the work.

sources.label: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, Kentucky State and National Scenic Byways and Highways
